marrow__ANAT_CH40_Q015.takeaway: Apical axillary nodes receive efferent drainage from the other axillary groups and pass it toward supraclavicular nodes.
marrow__ANAT_CH40_Q015.displayText: The apical group receives lymphatic drainage from the remaining axillary lymph-node groups and is therefore also called the terminal axillary lymph-node group. The source summarizes drainage as anterior, posterior and lateral groups -> central group -> apical group, followed by drainage to supraclavicular nodes.
emphasis: The apical group receives lymphatic drainage from the remaining axillary lymph-node groups and is therefore also called the terminal axillary lymph-node group
The source summarizes drainage as anterior, posterior and lateral groups -> central group -> apical group, followed by drainage to supraclavicular nodes

rationales.a: Central nodes collect from anterior, posterior and lateral groups but then drain onward to apical nodes.
rationales.c: Lateral/humeral nodes receive much of the upper-limb drainage and are upstream of central/apical groups.
rationales.d: Posterior/subscapular nodes are one of the groups that drain toward central nodes.

marrow__ANAT_CH40_Q016.takeaway: The lateral (humeral) nodes lie posteromedial to the axillary vein; lateral thoracic vessels accompany the anterior (pectoral) group.
marrow__ANAT_CH40_Q016.displayText: The false statement is that the lateral group lies along the lateral thoracic vessels. The source places the lateral/humeral group posteromedial to the axillary vein, while the anterior/pectoral group lies along the lateral thoracic vessels. Axillary lymph nodes collectively drain the entire upper limb, breast and trunk above the umbilicus. The source divides them into lateral/humeral, anterior/pectoral, posterior/subscapular, central and apical groups and tabulates their locations, afferents and efferents.

rationales.c: Apical nodes lie near the axillary vessels/apex.
